item.title: Deploy local AI via Ollama, Open-WebUI and VSCode/VSCodium
item.description:
This guide walks you through installing Ollama on a Linux system, serving it to a strictly local localhost WebUI (ensuring no exposure to the internet), and leveraging your local Large Language Models (LLMs) as an AI Chat Agent and autocomplete engine inside VSCode and/or VSCodium.

Why this setup?

  • No root / sudo required: Everything runs cleanly within your user space.
  • 100% Private: No reverse proxies or exposed external ports—just a local Python environment and standard tools.
  • Completely Free & Offline: No accounts, API keys, or data tracking required.

item.title: Avoid Python Package Import-Errors in VSCodium or VSCode
item.description:
If you are working with Conda environments, you might notice that VSCodium or VS Code shows “import not found” errors (red squiggly lines) even though your code runs perfectly fine in the terminal.

This happens because the IDE’s Python extension doesn’t automatically know which Conda environment to use for its background linting and IntelliSense. By explicitly setting the interpreter path, you tell the IDE exactly where to look for your installed packages.
